text:
emily-support: New escalation from Nate (ACME) — Dedicated eu-west2 pool 'acme-ded-1' reporting repeated 429s and p99 spikes (400ms -> 2s) since 2026-02-15 06:10 UTC. They're at ~70% of reserved throughput. Ticket INC-4321. Repro steps and logs below.

nate-cs: Client repro: steady rps ~45, median 150-200ms but tails to ~2s. GPU utilization on nodes shows 45-65% but memory alloc spikes and context-switches coincide with tails. Customer asks if this could be a noisy neighbor.

jon-ops: Can you paste a few request IDs + node_ids? I'll check scheduler, node assignments, and MIG layout.

nate-cs: Here are a few sample IDs from their run:
```
request_id,node_id
req_01a2,node-eu2-17
req_01a3,node-eu2-23
req_01b0,node-eu2-17
req_01c9,node-eu2-17
```

infra-bot: Autoscaler event: scale_down prevented at 2026-02-15T06:05:12Z due to pending requests. Pool 'acme-ded-1' node summary:
- node-eu2-17: A100-MIG partitions: 1g.5gbx6, GPU mem alloc spike observed (72%).
- node-eu2-23: A100-MIG partitions: 1g.5gbx4, avg util 48%.
Recent scheduler logs show repeated batcher placement on node-eu2-17.

mike-eng: If one node is getting denser batches or larger MIG partitions, it can cause p99 spikes for collocated workloads. Things to check: batcher affinity config, per-pool scheduler weights, and whether different model versions landed on the same MIG slice. Also confirm cgroup limits / CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES aren't being overridden.

priya-ml: We've seen this pattern when KV cache isn't collocated — requests that hit different nodes cause cache misses and long warmups. Quick repro and triage commands I usually ask the customer to run:
```bash
# from a small VM in eu-west2 to reproduce tail
for i in {1..50}; do \
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-base","input":"hello world"}' &\
done
wait
# then on the problematic host: nvidia-smi -q; cat /proc/$(pgrep -f model-server)/oom_score
```
Also check our KV eviction logs and prefix-cache misses in the console for that pool.

emily-support: I'll ask them to run the curl test and share the output + nvidia-smi -q for node-eu2-17. As a short-term mitigation I'm going to spin up a canary with the hot model pinned to a small isolated subset to see if tail improves. @jon-ops can you enable temporary isolation (label acme:isolated=true) and redeploy the pool with nodeAffinity?

jon-ops: :thumbsup: Will add the label and update the scheduler to honor node affinity for 'acme-ded-1'. I'll also audit MIG partitioning across the pool and consider increasing per-node MIG slices for this customer if we see imbalance. Marking INC-4321 as high priority and will follow up here with node assignment changes. (reaction :eyes:)

nate-cs: Thanks — forwarding these steps to the customer now. They appreciate the quick turnaround and will run the tests and share logs.
